parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility ban, border restriction, custody rule or documented police targeting is in the dossier; same-sex conduct is lawful and society is described as broadly neutral, with 85% in 2017 opposing violence. Conversely, no operating visitor-facing remedy, facility/custody/care practice, or recent trans-specific violence assessment is documented, and attitudes data are dated and largely sexuality-framed. Absence of resident legal gender recognition or anti-discrimination law is not a visitor exposure. This is reduced-to-elevated risk: no universal or organised exposure, but thin, uncertain protection.

entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No border guidance accepting foreign markers is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Not documented. No interaction between entry and detention or services is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific detention, search or custody-placement rule is documented; general police detentions in 2024 report have no trans content.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No individual-assessment or identity-based placement protocol is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Not documented. No documented route from investigation to custody placement.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. No identity-based facility-access protection is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not documented. City attitude differences are dated and sexuality-framed, with no current facility rule documented.

care_services.protection: Not documented. No visitor care-access shield or operating service remedy is documented.
care_services.interaction: Not documented. No interaction between care access and entry, custody or facilities is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No criminalisation of gender identity or trans presentation; no state threat-framing or targeting documented. Articles 191 and 160 cover incitement and aggravated homicide on gender-identity grounds.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Decriminalisation since 2015/2020 and 2017 court ruling permitting LGBT organisation registration indicate some institutional recognition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: No prosecution under Articles 191 or 160 is recorded, so the paper provisions are not shown operating for visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No age-dependent visitor, custody, care or facility rule is documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No travelling-family or minor-specific protection is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. No documented interaction between adult and minor treatment.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence figure or recent pattern is documented; a 2015 activist statement said the community was not targeted by violence as in some regional peers, but discrimination was real. Family ostracisation is resident-facing.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2017 survey: 85% opposed violence against LGBTQ people. No trans-specific prosecution or visitor remedy is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Not documented. No documented police response to a trans visitor victim.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory discrimination protection in education, health, housing or employment; employment protection was repealed effective 2024. No visitor complaint mechanism is documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts struck the moral-order registration clause in 2017, showing some rule-of-law capacity, but no visitor remedy outcome is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Resident-facing gaps do not document visitor document rejection or service denial; most journey-stage practices remain unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: lawful expression, no documented targeting, tolerant/neutral social record, no specialist visitor remedy, and open custody questions. This case lacks documented traditional acceptance and a compensation outcome, offset by actual decriminalisation.

Lower: 0.75-C documents community acceptance, identity-based facilities/wards, and an enforced compensation remedy. Here facilities, custody and remedies are not documented and attitude evidence is dated, so operating protection is not shown.

Higher: 0.55-A documents recurring visitor-facing refusals and threat-framing confrontations with partial remedies. No such recurring traveller-facing refusals, facility ban or police targeting are documented here.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national decriminalisation and neutral-to-tolerant attitudes remove the heaviest exposures—criminalisation, universal facility exclusion and organised targeting—while courts have shown some capacity to protect LGBT organisation status. However, no traveller-facing protection is documented as operating: Articles 191 and 160 have no recorded prosecutions, no anti-discrimination remedy exists, and entry, facilities, custody and care are undocumented. Dated, sexuality-framed surveys and resident discrimination indicate possible friction, not a documented visitor campaign. Hence 0.65, below anchors with proven remedies and above those with recurring visitor harms.
